selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main truth named in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the truth that Allah manages and governs creation.

questions.question: Which three broad parts of creation are mentioned together at the start?
questions.answer: The heavenly bodies, the natural elements, and the creatures living on earth.

questions.question: How is the whole world pictured after being managed this way?
questions.answer: It is pictured as an organized and beautiful place, like a well-run realm or palace.

questions.question: What is the benefit of saying they help one another?
questions.answer: It shows that creation works in harmony, not as disconnected pieces.

questions.question: What picture is used to explain the difficulty of this work?
questions.answer: The picture of a ruler managing a giant army made of many different groups.

questions.question: In that army example, what kinds of needs must be met for every group?
questions.answer: Their gear, clothing, instructions, release, and payment must all be handled properly.

questions.question: What qualities mark the ruler’s management in the comparison?
questions.answer: It is done completely, correctly, on time, without mistakes, delay, shortage, or confusion.

questions.question: What do people directly observe each spring, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They observe an unseen hand creating and managing a vast living army of many species.

questions.question: What happens to around three hundred thousand species in autumn?
questions.answer: They are released from service and die, as part of the cycle of life.

questions.question: What action stands at the center of this passage?
questions.answer: The central action is orderly governing and arranging creation.

questions.question: What contrast appears between the beings mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: The passage mentions both mighty things, like heavenly bodies and elements, and weak creatures on earth.

questions.question: What large parts of creation are governed together in this passage?
questions.answer: The skies, the natural forces, and the living beings on earth are governed together.

questions.question: Why does the passage move from the huge universe to spring on earth?
questions.answer: To show a clear, understandable example of the same truth on one visible page of creation.

questions.question: What is the purpose of comparing the world to a kingdom, city, and palace?
questions.answer: It highlights beauty, organization, and careful management.

questions.question: What must that ruler provide for each group?
questions.answer: He must give each one its own clothing, weapons, orders, release, and pay.

questions.question: Why can no other hand share in this administration, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because any interfering cause would upset the balance and create confusion.

questions.question: In the real example, who performs a similar work every spring?
questions.answer: An unseen hand performs it.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do we actually see every spring?
questions.answer: We see a hidden power bringing into being and organizing countless species like a vast army.

questions.question: What title is given to the truth explained in this section?
questions.answer: It is called the truth of disposing and administering.

questions.question: What words in the passage show that this rule is both strong and caring?
questions.answer: It describes the administration as powerful and also merciful.

questions.question: How are these different created things connected in the passage?
questions.answer: They are made to support one another and are directed together.

questions.question: What does the phrase about taking all necessary measures teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that everything needed for the system is carefully arranged.

questions.question: About how many different groups are in that army?
questions.answer: Four hundred thousand.

questions.question: What does the passage say proves the greatness of the commander in the comparison?
questions.answer: The fact that such a huge and detailed system is handled perfectly proves extraordinary power.
